1.4.1 Google Search for Known Vulnerabilities:
1.4.1.1 Neo4j Vulnerabilities and Exploits - {Findings: Several vulnerabilities have been identified over time, including Privilege Escalation, Path Traversal Vulnerabilities, XML External Entity (XXE) Vulnerabilities, Remote Code Execution (RCE), Access Control Flaws, and Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). Privilege Escalation: Notable issues include a significant problem in Neo4j 4.2.x where users could bypass security and gain full administrator-level access, and another privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2021-34802) in the Neo4j Graph Database. Path Traversal Vulnerabilities: The APOC library, an add-on for Neo4j, has been affected by path traversal vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-23532, CVE-2022-37423). XXE Vulnerabilities: APOC had an XXE vulnerability (CVE-2023-23926) in the apoc.import.graphml procedure. An earlier XXE vulnerability (CVE-2018-1000820) was also reported in Neo4j APOC Procedures. RCE: A critical RCE vulnerability (CVE-2021-34371) was identified in the Neo4j Database Server. Access Control Flaws: Incorrect access control in Neo4j Enterprise Database Server 3.4.x before 3.4.9 (CVE-2018-18389) could allow attackers to log in with arbitrary passwords. CSRF: Older versions like Neo4J 1.9.2 were vulnerable to CSRF (CVE-2013-7259). Security Best Practices: Neo4j emphasizes proactive security measures such as keeping software up-to-date, using strong passwords, implementing strict access controls, deploying on secure servers, encrypting data, using secure communication, restricting file system access, managing configuration files, monitoring for suspicious activity, using a proxy, and configuring the Content-Security-Policy header. Further References: Various resources for further information include Neo4j's official security advisories, security best practices/checklist, CVE databases, GitHub advisories, SecAlerts, and Neo4j's Trust
